images.caption: Front Street in Downtown Traverse City is a charming and vibrant commercial drag that is the symbolic and commercial heart of the Grand Traverse Bay region. Developed initially during the 19th Century

place.source_title: Front Street block with a long cream facade, Traverse City

brief: A long three-storey cream-painted commercial block with rows of arched windows, a bracketed cornice and shopfronts under flags. One photo. Older than 1970: Petoskey's Gaslight District (the town's model) is a row of 1880-1910 brick commercial blocks; no newer example of this main-street type exists. Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: a long Front Street block (Traverse City, 1890): a three-storey painted Italianate front with dozens of arched hooded windows and a bracketed cornice, a brick arcaded ground floor with awnings and blade signs, banners on the lamp posts

why.note: a single long Italianate block anchoring the street wall
